regulation tool of the mining sector
- New authorization procedure for mining works : - involving public enquiry, - environmental and socio-econonomic studies, - a special administrative police, - financial guarantees for environmental works - From 2012 to 2015, every existing mining site will go through this authorization procedure - 31 sites - Already heated debates on some locations (Thio) - The goal is to set individual administrative authorization, with technical prescriptions, rehabilitation objectives, etc.. - The “police des mines” is now in action: - Since 2009, 42 administrative order issued - 7 police report preliminary of judicial actions - - The “Rйserves Techniques Provinciales”, a legislative framework to secure resources, for future metallurgic development: - Used for the first time in February 2012 for Prony & Pernod An active mining cadastral system

to bring together opposite views on nickel
- In NC, the government and the provinces share responsibilities in the field of mining policy - Since 2010, regular meetings between elected representatives have been organized in order to build a common vision on what the industrial policy of NC should be. - A preliminary report has been drafted in 2012, based on extensive research: - The nickel resources inventory - Economic analysis of the added value of each development model - Technical analysis of the laterite processing technologies - Socio-economic work on the impact of mining - The work is under progress, in order to reach some kind of consensus. Extra technical work is being done: - The analysis of the nickel market in 2020 (Jim Lennon/Wood Mac Kenzy) - Preliminary assessment of the SMVRM - - The opportunity to discuss further those topics will be given by NC2025 A point of consensus : the necessity to preserve the
interests of the next generations through a sovereign
fund
- Many pacific Islands have built sovereign funds. All share similar situations: - Small population - Inequalities in the economic fabric - Isolation - Budget volatility - Nickel in NC has generated significant economic development but is a non-renewable resource. There is a widespread consensus on the necessity to preserve future generations from the risk of exhaustion. - A sovereign fund

could offer a solution. A first source of foreseen funding will be a mining royalty. Such a royalty doesn’t exist so far in New Caledonia, whereas it is widespread in mining countries Another point of consensus: exploring the other
resources
